answer: Optical hardware attestation limits Sybil attacks by binding each agent to a token containing random microscopic pigment particles. Nodes authenticate by measuring unique laser scattering along a spiral trajectory, ensuring adversaries cannot clone tokens or rekindle credentials from a dormant ember. An attacker must expend scarce, precision-fabricated physical substrates per identity. However, thermal expansion and surface wear can distort optical readings, falsely rejecting valid agents.
